set1.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which problem is specifically attached to topical neomycin?
opts: It frequently causes sensitization
Correct, and the class can also accumulate systemically.
It bleaches hair and clothing
That is benzoyl peroxide.
It causes hypopigmentation
That is azelaic acid.
It is inactivated by benzoyl peroxide
That interaction belongs to tretinoin.

set1.io: 4 — Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which body sites are named as more permeable to a topical drug?
opts: Shins, forearms, dorsal hands and neck
These are average to poorly penetrated sites, the shin especially, where skin is thin over bone but poorly perfused.
Scrotum, face, axilla and scalp
Correct. The scrotum, face, axilla and scalp have a thin stratum corneum, and the axilla is naturally occluded, so all four absorb far more drug than ordinary skin.
Palms, soles, knees and elbows
These are the thick, keratinized sites where penetration is poorest, which is the opposite of what is asked.
Back, chest, abdomen and buttocks
The trunk is ordinary-thickness skin with average penetration; the highly permeable sites are the thin or naturally occluded ones.

set1.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which retinoid is paired with Kaposi sarcoma?
opts: Adapalene
Adapalene is an acne agent notable for its stability.
Alitretinoin
Correct. Bexarotene is the one paired with T-cell lymphoma.
Bexarotene
Bexarotene is paired with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; alitretinoin is the one used for Kaposi sarcoma.
Tazarotene
Tazarotene is used for acne and psoriasis.

set1.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What are patients advised about washing in acne?
opts: Wash as often as possible to remove surface oils
Excessive scrubbing and washing is listed as a contributory factor, so this would worsen the disease.
Wash with a high pH soap several times daily, since a raised pH increases the activity of other topical agents
A high pH may degrade the activity of other agents and is less tolerable on the skin.
Avoid washing the affected area entirely while on treatment
Cleansing is part of non-pharmacologic therapy rather than something to avoid.
Do not wash too frequently; twice a day, balancing cleanliness against drying and irritation
Correct, and it adds that once rinsed off no active product remains on the skin.

set1.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which systemic corticosteroid is explicitly excluded from causing drug-induced acne?
opts: Prednisone
Prednisone is named elsewhere as an oral corticosteroid used in therapy, not as the exception here.
Dexamethasone
Dexamethasone is given as a treatment option, and is not the stated exception.
Methylprednisolone
This appears in the atopic dermatitis section, not as the exception.
Hydrocortisone
Correct. Hydrocortisone is the one systemic corticosteroid not associated with the acneiform eruption, its low potency being the likely reason.

set1.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set1.q: For which form of acne is a topical retinoid first line?
opts: Noninflammatory, comedonal acne
Correct, and for inflammatory acne it is often combined with other agents rather than used alone.
Nodular acne with scarring
That severity is where systemic therapy, including isotretinoin, is considered.
Acne associated with adrenal hyperactivity
Adrenal hyperactivity is addressed with low-dose oral corticosteroid therapy; the retinoid's first-line role is in comedonal disease.
Drug-induced acne from systemic corticosteroids
Drug-induced acne is managed by addressing the offending drug; the retinoid is first line in ordinary comedonal acne.

set1.io: 7 — Identify contraindications for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What warning is attached to polymyxin B?
opts: Avoid using it on open wounds or denuded skin in high doses, because of neurotoxicity and nephrotoxicity risk
Correct. Loss of the barrier is what turns a topical agent into a systemic exposure.
Avoid it in pregnancy and in breastfeeding, because systemic absorption through inflamed skin is teratogenic
Teratogenicity is the concern with retinoids and tetracyclines; the polymyxin B warning is neurotoxicity and nephrotoxicity from systemic absorption through broken skin.
Avoid it in children under eight because it stains teeth
That restriction belongs to the tetracyclines.
Avoid it with benzoyl peroxide because it is inactivated
That interaction is tretinoin with benzoyl peroxide.

set1.io: 7 — Identify contraindications for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which patient should avoid topical tacrolimus or pimecrolimus?
opts: A patient with a weakened immune system
Correct. These calcineurin inhibitors suppress local T cell activity, so they are avoided where immunity is already weakened, with a possible cancer risk noted alongside.
A patient with a history of acne
Acne is not a stated contraindication for these agents.
A patient over the age of sixty
Age alone is not given as a bar.
A patient using an emollient
Emollients are part of routine care and are not a conflict.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: How does bacitracin work, and what is true of its systemic toxicity?
opts: It is a peptide antibiotic that prevents cell wall synthesis, and it has no systemic toxicity
Correct, with allergic dermatitis noted only rarely.
It binds bacterial transfer RNA to stop protein synthesis, and it accumulates systemically
That mechanism is mupirocin's, and bacitracin is the one with no systemic toxicity.
It interrupts the cytoplasmic membrane, and it risks nephrotoxicity
That describes polymyxin B.
It inhibits protein synthesis, and it frequently causes sensitization
That describes the topical aminoglycosides, neomycin in particular.

set1.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: A patient asks about the ciclopirox nail lacquer for onychomycosis. What is true of how well it works?
opts: It is less than twelve percent effective
Correct, and saying so up front is what keeps expectations honest for a months-long treatment.
It is curative in the majority of patients
Cure rates are low, under twelve percent, because the lacquer penetrates the nail plate poorly to reach fungus in the nail bed.
It works only on fingernails, not toenails
It is marketed for both fingernails and toenails; the limitation is its low cure rate, not the site.
It is as effective as oral terbinafine
No such comparison is made, and the stated efficacy is low.

set1.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Why is an azole sometimes combined with a corticosteroid?
opts: To make the preparation less irritating to the skin
Local irritation is listed as the adverse reaction, but symptom relief is the stated reason.
For more rapid symptom relief
Correct. The steroid addresses symptoms while the antifungal addresses the organism.
To prevent the development of resistance
Resistance is raised for erythromycin in acne, not as the reason for this combination.
To allow a shorter total course of therapy
The course remains prolonged either way; the steroid is added for faster relief of itch and inflammation, not to shorten treatment.

set1.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which laboratory change is listed among isotretinoin's adverse reactions?
opts: Reduced white cell count
Isotretinoin does not suppress the white cell count; the laboratory change to watch is a rise in serum lipids.
Increased serum lipids
Correct, and it sits alongside retinoid dermatitis, photophobia, arthralgia, headaches, alopecia and brittle nails.
Reduced serum calcium
No calcium effect is described for isotretinoin.
Raised serum immunoglobulin E
Raised immunoglobulin E is a minor indicator of atopic dermatitis.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What are the two proposed actions of azelaic acid?
opts: Conversion to benzoic acid within the stratum corneum together with a direct comedolytic peeling effect
That is benzoyl peroxide's route.
Inhibition of T cell activation and mast cell stabilization
That is the topical immunomodulator mechanism.
Antimicrobial activity and inhibition of the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
Correct. Azelaic acid is antimicrobial against Propionibacterium acnes and inhibits the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone, although its mechanism is not fully established.
Inhibition of fungal cell wall formation and keratinolysis
Fungal cell wall inhibition belongs to the azole antifungals.

set1.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which two problems are attached to intralesional steroid injection of an inflammatory nodule?
opts: Bleaching of hair and clothing, together with staining of the surrounding skin at the injection site
That belongs to benzoyl peroxide.
Photosensitivity and severe sunburn
That belongs to the topical retinoids.
Systemic absorption leading to adrenal suppression, and local tissue atrophy
Correct. Both are consequences of injecting a steroid into the lesion.
Permanent hyperpigmentation and keloid formation
Neither follows from the injection; the concerns are systemic absorption with adrenal suppression and local tissue atrophy at the site.

set1.io: 4 — Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What is true of nystatin's absorption?
opts: It is well absorbed orally and distributes widely
Nystatin is not absorbed from the gut at all, which is exactly why oral suspension works against candidal infection of the mouth and intestine without systemic exposure.
It is absorbed only through inflamed skin
Inflamed skin absorbs more of most topical drugs, but nystatin is characterized by essentially no absorption, which is what keeps it safe.
It accumulates systemically with repeated use
Systemic accumulation is raised for the topical aminoglycosides.
It has no oral absorption
Correct, which is why it is used for cutaneous and mucosal candidal infection rather than systemically.

set1.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: A parent asks what to do at home for a child with atopic dermatitis. Which set matches the non-pharmacologic advice?
opts: Hot baths to open the pores, followed by air drying
Baths are specified as lukewarm, and a lubricant is applied after.
Frequent washing with a high pH soap
That advice belongs to the acne cleansing discussion, and even there frequent washing is discouraged.
Frequent hot baths with a high pH soap, air drying afterwards, and occlusive dressings left on overnight
Occlusion is discussed as a variable in topical drug delivery, not as home care for children.
Lukewarm baths with lubricant applied afterwards, short fingernails, and avoiding overheating
Correct. Lukewarm water avoids stripping lipid, a lubricant seals in the moisture, short nails limit the damage from scratching, and overheating provokes itch.

set1.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: A patient on imiquimod reports redness, swelling and erosions at the site. What is true of this?
opts: Skin irritation occurs in virtually all patients, and the degree of inflammation parallels efficacy
Correct, so the reaction is expected and is not by itself a reason to stop.
It indicates an allergic reaction and the drug should be stopped
The inflammation is the drug working rather than an allergy; imiquimod is an immune response modifier, and the local reaction is how it clears the lesion.
It is unusual and suggests secondary bacterial infection
Irritation occurs in virtually all patients rather than being unusual.
It means the applied dose is too low and the frequency should be increased until the skin clears
The reaction indicates an active immune response rather than an inadequate dose; increasing it would only worsen the erosion.

set1.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which two properties are used to distinguish adapalene from tretinoin?
opts: Adapalene is used only for psoriasis rather than acne
Tazarotene is the retinoid used for both acne and psoriasis; adapalene is distinguished by its stability in light and with benzoyl peroxide.
Adapalene must be applied only at night because it is photolabile
This describes tretinoin; adapalene is the photostable one, which is precisely what separates them.
Adapalene is stable in sunlight and stable with benzoyl peroxide
Correct, and it also tends to be less irritating.
Adapalene is a systemic agent and requires pregnancy testing
Adapalene is a topical retinoid; the pregnancy program belongs to isotretinoin.

set1.io: 8 — Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions
set1.q: Which interaction is described between benzoyl peroxide and tretinoin?
opts: Tretinoin prevents benzoyl peroxide from converting to benzoic acid
The direction is the reverse: benzoyl peroxide inactivates tretinoin, which is why adapalene, stable alongside it, is preferred in combination.
The two together cause systemic hypervitaminosis A
No systemic vitamin A toxicity is described from this pairing.
Benzoyl peroxide inactivates tretinoin
Correct, and it is why adapalene, which is stable with benzoyl peroxide, is highlighted separately.
Benzoyl peroxide increases tretinoin absorption to toxic levels
Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes and inactivates tretinoin rather than increasing its absorption, so the pair applied together does less, not more.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which three actions are attributed to topical retinoic acid?
opts: Converts to benzoic acid after penetration, bleaches surface pigment, and suppresses sebum production
Conversion to benzoic acid is benzoyl peroxide.
Inhibits fungal ergosterol, reduces scaling, and stimulates interferon
Ergosterol inhibition is the allylamines and interferon stimulation is imiquimod.
Corrects abnormal follicular keratinization, reduces Propionibacterium acnes counts, and reduces inflammation
Correct. Retinoic acid normalizes follicular keratinization so the plug does not form, lowers Propionibacterium acnes counts and damps inflammation, which is why it covers both lesion types.
Dissolves existing comedones, blocks androgen receptors, and thins the epidermis
Androgen receptor blockade belongs to the antiandrogen section.

set1.io: 9 — List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: An exacerbation warrants a medium to high potency corticosteroid. What should be done next?
opts: Continue it indefinitely to prevent relapse
Continuing at potency is what produces atrophy, striae and adrenal suppression; the strength is stepped down once the flare settles.
Stop abruptly once the flare settles and use nothing further
Stopping outright invites rebound; the potency is stepped down to a lower agent rather than withdrawn completely.
Add an oral corticosteroid for the same duration
Oral corticosteroids are a separate short-course option, not a routine addition.
Use it for one to two weeks, then switch to a lower potency
Correct. The step-down is the protocol rather than continuing at strength.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What is mupirocin's mechanism?
opts: It prevents bacterial cell wall synthesis
That is bacitracin.
It interrupts the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane
That is polymyxin B.
It inhibits fungal ergosterol production and so prevents cell wall synthesis
That is the allylamines.
It binds bacterial transfer RNA, preventing protein synthesis
Correct. Mupirocin inhibits isoleucyl transfer RNA synthetase, halting bacterial protein synthesis; it is not absorbed systemically, though it can irritate mucous membranes.

set1.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set1.q: How is topical therapy separated from systemic therapy in acne?
opts: Topical for the face, systemic for the trunk
Site is not what determines the route here.
Topical for mild to moderate disease, systemic for moderate to severe
Correct. Severity is what moves a patient onto systemic therapy.
Topical for inflammatory disease, systemic for comedonal disease
This inverts it; comedonal disease is where topical retinoid therapy is first line.
Topical for adults, systemic for adolescents
Age does not set the route; severity does, with topical therapy for mild to moderate and systemic for moderate to severe disease.

set1.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which conditions make up the atopic triad that atopic dermatitis belongs to?
opts: Urticaria and angioedema
These are not the two conditions named.
Acne vulgaris and rosacea
Acne and rosacea are pilosebaceous disorders with no atopic basis; the triad is eczema, asthma and allergic rhino-conjunctivitis.
Asthma and allergic rhino-conjunctivitis
Correct. The three share an atopic tendency to immunoglobulin E mediated inflammation, and in the skin a defective barrier is the major contributor.
Psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis
Psoriasis is immune-mediated but not atopic, and seborrheic dermatitis relates to Malassezia; neither belongs to the triad.

set1.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which two agents are named as allylamines, and how do they work?
opts: Ciclopirox and sertaconazole, which block precursor uptake
Ciclopirox blocks precursor uptake but is not an allylamine, and sertaconazole is an azole.
Naftifine and terbinafine, which inhibit ergosterol production and prevent cell wall synthesis
Correct, with local irritation as the adverse reaction.
Clotrimazole and miconazole, which inhibit fungal cytochrome P450
Those are azoles.
Nystatin and tolnaftate, which bind fungal membrane sterols directly and cause leakage of cell contents
Those are grouped separately under other antifungals.

set1.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What does bacterial lipase do in the acne cascade?
opts: Digests the sebaceous gland basement membrane
Lipase acts on sebum triglycerides, not on basement membrane; the free fatty acids it releases are what irritate the follicle.
Hydrolyses triglycerides into free fatty acids
Correct, and those free fatty acids feed the increase in keratinization and microcomedone formation.
Cleaves keratin so the follicular plug loosens
Keratinization increases in acne rather than being broken down; the plug forms rather than loosening.
Converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
That conversion appears under azelaic acid's proposed mechanism, not bacterial lipase.

set1.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Which vehicle is placed at the most drying end of its range, and which at the least?
opts: Powders are the most drying and lotions the least
Powders are within the list but tinctures anchor the drying end.
Tinctures are the most drying and ointments the least
Correct. The list runs tinctures, wet dressings, lotions, gels, aerosols, powders, pastes, creams, foams, ointments.
Ointments are the most drying and tinctures the least
This reverses the range: tinctures are alcohol-based and most drying, while ointments are the greasiest and least drying.
Creams are the most drying and gels the least
Both sit in the middle of the range rather than at its ends.

set1.io: 4 — Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of dermatologic drugs
set1.q: A patient's corticosteroid is not controlling a plaque. Based on the concentration gradient principle, what is predicted?
opts: Changing to a more drying vehicle will matter more than concentration
Vehicle matters, but it is a separate variable; the concentration gradient is what this principle predicts.
Only a change to a systemic agent will overcome it
Systemic therapy is reserved for moderate-severe disease, not for a single unresponsive plaque.
Raising the concentration increases drug transfer and can overcome the resistance
Correct. Absorption across the stratum corneum is driven by the concentration gradient, so a higher concentration drives more drug into the skin and can overcome apparent resistance.
Concentration has little effect once the stratum corneum is saturated
The gradient keeps driving transfer; increasing the concentration increases the amount of drug crossing rather than reaching a plateau.

set1.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: Why does an oral corticosteroid course for atopic dermatitis need a tapering dose?
opts: To avoid precipitating drug-induced acne
Drug-induced acne is discussed under acne and is not the reason for the taper here.
To allow the topical steroid to be started safely
No such sequencing requirement is described.
To reduce the risk of secondary infection
Treating secondary infection is a separate goal of therapy.
To prevent a flare-up
Correct. The taper protects against rebound rather than against withdrawal symptoms alone.

set1.io: 7 — Identify contraindications for dermatologic drugs
set1.q: What is true of isotretinoin and pregnancy?
opts: It is contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and men should avoid it as well
Correct, and the iPledge program exists around exactly this risk.
It is safe in the second and third trimesters, and only the first trimester requires contraceptive cover
It is contraindicated, without a safe window.
It is contraindicated only in the first trimester
There is no safe trimester; isotretinoin is teratogenic throughout, which is why contraception is required before, during and after the course.
It requires no pregnancy precautions because it is applied topically
Isotretinoin here is the systemic retinoid, not a topical agent.

set2.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which set gives the MAJOR indicators of atopic dermatitis?
opts: Edema, vesicles, erosions and ulcers at sites where a topical immunomodulator was applied
Edema, vesicles, erosions and ulcers describe the local inflammation imiquimod causes, not atopic dermatitis indicators.
Comedones, papulopustular lesions, and nodules
Comedones, papulopustular lesions and nodules are the noninflammatory and inflammatory lesions of acne, not atopic dermatitis indicators.
Pruritus, rash in areas typical of the disease, chronic or repeated symptoms, and family history
Correct. Raised immunoglobulin E, positive skin tests, dry patchy scales and infection susceptibility are the minor ones.
Raised immunoglobulin E, positive allergy skin tests, and dry patchy scales
These are listed as minor indicators rather than major ones.

set2.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Why should topical acne therapy be applied to the whole affected area rather than to individual spots?
opts: Spot application increases the risk of systemic absorption
Whole-area application increases the treated surface, so it would if anything raise absorption; the reason is that untreated follicles keep forming microcomedones.
The vehicle is only stable when spread thinly over a wide area
Vehicle stability is a formulation consideration, not the reason for whole-area application.
Individual lesions are already resolving by the time they are visible
Visible lesions are the end of a process that began weeks earlier, so treating only them leaves the forming microcomedones untouched.
Topical therapy only works where it is applied
Correct, and that is why the whole affected area is treated rather than visible lesions alone.

set2.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set2.q: How are acne lesions divided?
opts: Noninflammatory as open and closed comedones; inflammatory as papulopustular and nodular lesions
Correct. That split is what decides whether topical or systemic therapy is chosen.
Noninflammatory as papules; inflammatory as comedones
This reverses the two categories.
Superficial as pustular; deep as comedonal
The division is by inflammation rather than depth, because that is what decides between topical and systemic therapy.
Acute disease as nodular and pustular lesions; chronic disease as open and closed comedones alone
Acne is a chronic disease throughout; the useful division is inflammatory against noninflammatory, not acute against chronic.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What is the mechanism of the topical azole antifungals?
opts: They inhibit ergosterol production directly
The allylamines inhibit squalene epoxidase to block ergosterol synthesis directly; the azoles act earlier, through fungal cytochrome P450.
They inhibit uptake of molecular precursors at the fungal cell wall
That is ciclopirox.
They bind fungal transfer RNA to stop protein synthesis
No topical antifungal works by binding transfer RNA; that is mupirocin's antibacterial mechanism.
They inhibit fungal cytochrome P450, preventing cell wall formation
Correct, and the named agents are clotrimazole, ketoconazole, miconazole and sertaconazole.

set2.io: 7 — Identify contraindications for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which patient should not be given a topical retinoid?
opts: A patient taking an oral contraceptive
Oral contraceptives are listed as a useful acne therapy in some women, not a conflict.
A patient over sixty years of age
Age is no bar; topical retinoids are used in older patients for wrinkles and dyspigmentation as well as for acne.
A patient who is pregnant
Correct. Retinoids are vitamin A derivatives and teratogenic, so they are avoided in pregnancy even by the topical route.
A patient with a history of eczema
Eczema is not given as a contraindication to topical retinoid therapy.

set2.io: 4 — Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What is the depot effect, and what does it allow?
opts: Repeated applications saturate hair follicles and shut down absorption
The depot effect prolongs availability rather than stopping absorption.
Skin acts as a reservoir for the drug, which may permit once daily dosing of short acting drugs
Correct. The reservoir is what lets a short acting drug be given less often than its half-life suggests.
The drug is stored in subcutaneous fat and released during exercise, which is why activity increases absorption
The reservoir is the stratum corneum itself rather than adipose tissue, and release is steady rather than exercise-dependent.
The vehicle evaporates and leaves crystals that dissolve slowly in sweat
Nothing crystallizes in sweat; the drug binds within the stratum corneum, which then releases it gradually.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Why is a sedating antihistamine included in the non-pharmacologic advice for a child with atopic dermatitis?
opts: To reverse the skin barrier dysfunction
Barrier dysfunction is addressed by lubricants and hydration, not antihistamines.
To treat the secondary skin infections
Secondary infection is treated with an antibacterial agent; the antihistamine is chosen for its sedating effect on night-time itch.
To lower serum immunoglobulin E
Nothing here is aimed at lowering immunoglobulin E; the antihistamine is used for its sedative effect on night-time scratching.
To reduce night-time itching
Correct. The sedating property is being used for the itch that disrupts sleep.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which agents are the gold standard for atopic dermatitis?
opts: Sedating antihistamines
These address night-time itching rather than the disease itself.
Topical corticosteroids
Correct, with the agent chosen by severity and by site of disease.
Topical immunomodulators
Tacrolimus and pimecrolimus are named as second line, after topical steroids.
Oral corticosteroids
These are used for short courses during exacerbations rather than as the standard.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which use is given for mupirocin beyond ordinary skin infection?
opts: Eliminating nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus
Correct, and its coverage is most gram positive aerobes, especially meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
Eliminating vulvovaginal candidiasis in women
That indication belongs to the azole antifungals.
Treating recurrent orolabial herpes simplex
That is acyclovir and penciclovir.
Treating onychomycosis of the toenails
That is the ciclopirox nail lacquer.

set2.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which topical antibiotic is named as the preferred agent for acne, and what is happening to the alternative?
opts: Mupirocin is the preferred agent for acne; bacitracin is losing efficacy to Propionibacterium acnes resistance
Those two belong to the other topical antibiotics section, not to acne.
Neomycin is preferred; polymyxin B is losing efficacy
Neomycin is noted for causing sensitization and is not the acne agent.
Clindamycin is preferred; erythromycin is losing efficacy to Propionibacterium acnes resistance
Correct, and both are noted to lack systemic side effects.
Erythromycin is preferred; clindamycin is losing efficacy to resistance
This reverses the two: clindamycin is preferred, and it is erythromycin whose usefulness is being eroded by Propionibacterium acnes resistance.

set2.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Occlusion increases efficacy. What must be flagged alongside that?
opts: It reliably shortens the required duration of therapy
Occlusion increases the amount absorbed rather than shortening the course; the trade-off is greater toxicity.
It prevents the vehicle from exerting any therapeutic effect of its own
A vehicle can be therapeutic in its own right, by hydrating or drying the skin, and occlusion does not remove that.
It makes regional variation in penetration irrelevant
Regional variation remains a separate major variable.
It raises the question of increased toxicity as well
Correct. Occlusion hydrates the stratum corneum and drives more drug in, so systemic absorption and local adverse effects rise along with efficacy.

set2.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: A patient develops pustular inflammation on the trunk a few weeks after starting a systemic corticosteroid. What happens when the steroid is stopped?
opts: No change, because the eruption is independent of the drug
The eruption is drug-induced, and its course follows the drug: stopping it provokes an initial flare as inflammation rebounds.
An initial worsening, because inflammation increases
Correct, and warning the patient of this in advance is what stops them abandoning the plan.
Immediate and complete resolution of the eruption
Withdrawal removes the steroid's immunosuppression, so the eruption flares before it settles rather than clearing at once.
Conversion of the pustules into open comedones
This transformation is not described.

set2.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which systemic effects are attributed to topical corticosteroids?
opts: Raised serum lipids and brittle nails
Those belong to systemic isotretinoin.
Photosensitivity, severe sunburn, desquamation, burning and stinging that decrease with continued use
That is the topical retinoid profile.
Adrenal suppression, infections, hyperglycemia, glaucoma, cataracts and growth retardation in children
Correct. That a topical agent can do all of this is the point of the potency and duration warnings.
Hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity
Neuro and nephrotoxicity are raised for polymyxin B on denuded skin, not for steroids.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which organism is named as proliferating in the anaerobic conditions created by pooled sebum?
opts: Staphylococcus aureus
Staphylococcus aureus is a skin pathogen but is aerobic and is not the organism of the acne follicle.
Malassezia furfur
Malassezia furfur is a yeast, responsible for pityriasis versicolor rather than for acne.
Streptococcus pyogenes
Streptococcus pyogenes causes impetigo and cellulitis, not the anaerobic colonization of the pilosebaceous unit.
Propionibacterium acnes
Correct. Pooled sebum creates anaerobic conditions in which this organism proliferates.

set2.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which adverse effect of benzoyl peroxide most needs to be raised with a patient before they start it?
opts: It stains the skin orange for the duration of therapy
Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizing agent that bleaches rather than stains, which is why it ruins colored towels and bedding.
It can bleach hair, clothing and bedding
Correct. This is the practical warning that prevents a patient ruining clothes and abandoning the drug.
It causes a permanent blue-gray discoloration of the skin
The discoloration is bleaching of hair and fabric rather than any permanent change in skin pigment.
It commonly causes systemic hypersensitivity reactions
The adverse effects are local irritation of skin and mucous membranes; systemic hypersensitivity is not a feature.

set2.io: 9 — List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: How often is imiquimod applied?
opts: Two to five times per week
Correct, which is a weekly schedule rather than a daily one.
Twice daily without interruption
That schedule belongs to azelaic acid once titrated up.
Once monthly
Monthly application is far too infrequent to sustain the local immune response; imiquimod is applied two to five times per week.
Only at night, because it is photolabile
Photolability is tretinoin's property.

set2.io: 7 — Identify contraindications for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which two groups are contraindicated from receiving tetracyclines?
opts: Children under eight years and pregnant women
Correct. Tetracyclines chelate calcium and deposit in developing teeth and bone, staining teeth permanently in children under eight and crossing the placenta in pregnancy.
Adolescents and the elderly
Adolescents are the population most often treated for acne, not a contraindicated group.
Patients with eczema and patients with psoriasis
Neither condition is given as a contraindication to tetracyclines.
Patients taking oral contraceptives and patients on spironolactone
Both are acne therapies rather than contraindications; the contraindicated groups are children under eight and pregnant women.

set2.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which pigmentary adverse effect is attached to azelaic acid?
opts: Hypopigmentation
Correct. It is listed with mild skin irritation and dryness.
Hyperpigmentation of sun-exposed areas
Azelaic acid lightens rather than darkens the skin, which is why it is also used for post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.
Slate-gray discoloration of the nail beds
This is not described for azelaic acid.
Yellow staining of the sclera
No ocular pigment change is attributed to this agent.

set2.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which antiandrogen is named for acne?
opts: Ketoconazole
Ketoconazole appears here as a topical azole antifungal.
Cyproterone
Cyproterone is an antiandrogen used elsewhere, but spironolactone is the agent used for acne here.
Spironolactone
Correct. Spironolactone blocks the androgen receptor, reducing sebum production, and is available as a gel as well as orally.
Finasteride
Finasteride inhibits five-alpha-reductase and is used for androgenetic alopecia and prostatic hyperplasia rather than acne.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What happens to benzoyl peroxide after it penetrates the stratum corneum?
opts: It remains unchanged in the skin and works purely by oxidizing sebum within the follicle
It does not act unchanged; it crosses the stratum corneum and is then converted to benzoic acid, which is the antibacterial form.
It is converted to benzoic acid, which is active against Propionibacterium acnes
Correct. It crosses unchanged and is converted once through.
It is converted to salicylic acid, which is keratinolytic
Salicylic acid is a separate keratinolytic agent; benzoyl peroxide is converted to benzoic acid.
It is converted to retinoic acid, which corrects keratinization
Retinoic acid is the acid form of vitamin A and belongs to the retinoid section.

set2.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: A patient is starting a topical azole. What should they be told about duration?
opts: Treatment must continue for at least six months
Six months applies to oral treatment of nail infection; a topical azole for skin runs two to three weeks.
Treatment is generally prolonged, on the order of two to three weeks
Correct, and stopping early is how a treated infection returns.
A single application is usually curative
A single application cannot clear a dermatophyte from the stratum corneum; two to three weeks of continuous treatment is needed.
Treatment continues until the rash disappears, then stops immediately
Stopping when the rash clears leaves viable fungus in the stratum corneum, which is why the course runs a set two to three weeks.

set2.io: 5 — Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which of these is a LOCAL adverse effect of topical steroids, rather than a systemic one?
opts: Adrenal suppression
Adrenal suppression follows systemic absorption through the skin and is a systemic effect; the local ones are atrophy, acne, rosacea and vehicle allergy.
Cataracts
Cataracts are listed as systemic, alongside glaucoma.
Growth retardation in children
Growth retardation reflects systemic absorption in children; the local effects are confined to the treated skin.
Skin atrophy
Correct. Local effects are skin atrophy, acne, rosacea and allergic dermatitis related to the vehicle.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: A lesion is oozing, vesicular and crusting. Which end of the vehicle range is paired with that presentation?
opts: The middle of the range, regardless of the lesion
The vehicle is matched to the lesion rather than defaulting to the middle; a wet lesion takes a drying vehicle.
Vehicle choice is not linked to lesion morphology
Morphology drives vehicle choice directly: wet lesions take drying vehicles and dry, scaly lesions take greasy ones.
The drying end of the range
Correct. Oozing, vesiculation and crusting are matched to drying vehicles; scaling, lichenification and xerosis to the least drying.
The least drying end of the range
That end is paired with scaling, lichenification and xerosis, which is the opposite presentation.

set2.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Most topical acne agents cause skin irritation. What does that lead to, and how should therapy be started?
opts: It confirms the drug is working, so maintain the starting strength
Irritation is a barrier to adherence rather than a sign of efficacy, and holding the starting strength is what makes patients stop.
It requires an immediate switch to systemic therapy, because irritation means the topical agent has failed
Severity, not irritation, is what moves a patient to systemic therapy.
It is prevented entirely by using an alcoholic solution
Alcoholic solutions are more irritating, not less; a non-alcoholic vehicle is the option to consider when irritation is a problem.
It can lead to patient discontinuation, so start with lower strength and increase gradually
Correct. Anticipating the irritation is what keeps a patient on therapy.

set2.io: 10 — Outline appropriate patient education for dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Why should tretinoin be applied at night?
opts: It is photolabile
Correct. Being degraded by light is the reason for nightly application, distinct from the photosensitivity it also causes.
Sebum production peaks overnight
Sebum timing is not the issue; tretinoin is degraded by light, so daytime application destroys the drug.
It stains clothing if applied during the day
Bleaching of clothing belongs to benzoyl peroxide.
It must be applied at the same time as benzoyl peroxide
Benzoyl peroxide inactivates tretinoin, so they are not applied together.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What is the anti-inflammatory action of tetracyclines in acne?
opts: They stimulate macrophages to release tumor necrosis factor alpha
That is imiquimod's mechanism.
They chelate calcium ions, which prevents neutrophil and monocyte chemotaxis
Correct. That is an anti-inflammatory action separate from killing the organism.
They stabilize mast cell membranes and block histamine release
Mast cell activation is addressed by the topical immunomodulators.
They inhibit the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone
That is proposed for azelaic acid.

set2.io: 1 — Identify dermatologic drug classes and commonly prescribed dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which agent is placed in class 1, superpotent?
opts: Triamcinolone acetonide cream
Triamcinolone acetonide cream sits in class 5, mid-strength; clobetasol propionate is the class 1 superpotent agent.
Clobetasol propionate
Correct, listed in class 1 in cream, ointment, lotion, spray, shampoo and foam forms.
Hydrocortisone
Hydrocortisone sits at the least potent end of the chart.
Desonide
Desonide lotion appears in class 5, lower mid-strength.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What are acyclovir and penciclovir used for topically, and what kind of molecule are they?
opts: Recurrent orolabial herpes simplex infection; they are synthetic guanine analogs
Correct, active against herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2.
External and perianal warts; they are immunomodulators
That is imiquimod.
Vulvovaginal candidiasis; they are azoles
That is the azole antifungal indication.
Actinic keratoses and superficial basal cell carcinoma; they are topical retinoid preparations
Actinic keratosis is treated with imiquimod or fluorouracil; acyclovir and penciclovir are guanine analogs active against herpes simplex.

set2.io: 3 — Identify indications for commonly used dermatologic drugs
set2.q: Which gap in coverage is flagged for tolnaftate?
opts: It has no activity below the stratum corneum
Depth is not the issue; the gap is organism coverage, since tolnaftate treats dermatophytes but not Candida.
It has no activity on the scalp
Site is not the stated gap.
It has no Candida activity
Correct. Tolnaftate covers dermatophytes but has no activity against Candida, so a candidal intertrigo needs nystatin or an azole instead.
It has no dermatophyte activity
Dermatophyte infection is what it is used for.

set2.io: 2 — Describe the molecular mechanism of action of dermatologic drugs
set2.q: What does imiquimod do?
opts: It stimulates peripheral mononuclear cells to release interferon alpha and macrophages to produce tumor necrosis factor alpha and interleukins
Correct. It is an immunomodulator rather than a directly cytotoxic agent.
It inhibits T cell, mast cell and keratinocyte activation
That is tacrolimus and pimecrolimus, which suppress rather than stimulate.
It is converted to benzoic acid after crossing the stratum corneum
That is benzoyl peroxide.
It corrects abnormal follicular keratinization, reduces bacterial counts within the follicle, and dampens the inflammatory response
That is a topical retinoid action.
